request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log. All 4 Playwright tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V30__claim_log.sql`, adds a `claim_log` table. Each row holds the status, the user, the sheet's today at the time, and the due, in the order the changes happened.
- **Server:**
  - A new `ClaimLogEntry` class holds one log line, and `Claim` loads its log along with the claim.
  - `ClaimService` writes a line when a claim is added (DRAFT) and on every status change: open, settle, PENDING, approve, reject, void and bulk open.
  - The due written is the one the claim shows at that moment, after the new status is applied. So a settled line has the due fixed at settling, and any late charge is included. It reads `n/a` when the claim has no rate.
- **Front end:** the claim response now includes `log`. Each claim row lists one `claim-log-line` per entry, oldest first, as `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`.

Moving a claim to another person doesn't change its status, so it adds no log line. Editing a draft doesn't either, so the DRAFT line keeps the due the claim had when it was added. The new table starts empty, so any claims already stored would show an empty log. Since the database is in memory and starts empty on each run, this doesn't affect anything now.
